images.title: Lali faces the rising Sun
images.purpose: Show from above what facing the rising Sun means: the girl faces east, her left hand points north, her right hand points south and west is behind her.
images.composition: A girl seen from directly above stands at the centre with her arms stretched up and down the frame, facing the right where the rising Sun is; four labelled arrows point away from her; a small compass card is in the top left corner.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, flat colours, thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px). Seen from directly above, with north at the top of the frame. LALI, ONE girl drawn as a plan view at the centre: her shoulders and stretched out arms are ONE straight vertical bar, 24 px wide and 300 px tall, at x 640 from y 258 to y 558, filled teal #0072B2; her head is ONE circle 76 px wide at the centre (x 640 and y 408) filled reddish purple #CC79A7, with ONE small white triangle (20 px long) on its right side pointing right as her nose, so she faces the right of the frame; her two hands are TWO white circles (36 px wide), one at the top end of the bar (x 640 and y 258) and one at the bottom end (x 640 and y 558). Because she faces right, her left hand is the top one and her right hand is the bottom one. THE RISING SUN is ONE amber #E69F00 circle 140 px wide, centre x 1250 and y 408, with EIGHT short straight rays (each 34 px long and 8 px thick, amber) round it at equal spacing, outside the circle. The Sun is on the right of the frame, in front of her. FOUR DIRECTION ARROWS, each a green #009E73 line 8 px thick with one arrow head, start close to her and point away from her: East from x 700 to x 1000 at y 408 (pointing right, towards the Sun), West from x 580 to x 380 at y 408 (pointing left), North from y 236 to y 150 at x 640 (pointing up) and South from y 580 to y 666 at x 640 (pointing down). LABELS in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (36 px): North centred at x 640 and y 112, above the north arrow head; East centred at x 850 and y 366, above the east arrow; South centred at x 640 and y 714, below the south arrow head; West centred at x 480 and y 366, above the west arrow; Left hand at x 800 and y 258, to the right of the top hand; Right hand at x 805 and y 558, to the right of the bottom hand; Lali at x 745 and y 466, below the east arrow and to the right of the head; Rising Sun centred at x 1250 and y 540, below the Sun. COMPASS CARD in the top left corner: a square card with rounded corners (corner radius 14 px), 170 by 170 px, from x 40 to x 210 and from y 40 to y 210, white fill, dark #2B2B2B outline 6 px, with a cross of two thin double headed dark arrows (4 px) inside it: one vertical from y 95 to y 155 at x 125 and one horizontal from x 96 to x 154 at y 125; the letter N in dark bold (38 px) centred at x 125 and y 72 (top), S in dark bold at x 125 and y 178 (bottom), W in dark bold at x 66 and y 125 (left) and E in red #D55E00 bold at x 184 and y 125 (right). In all: 1 girl, 1 Sun with 8 rays, 4 arrows, 8 word labels, 1 compass card. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the girl facing any way other than the right of the frame
the hand labels swapped: the top hand must be Left hand and the bottom hand must be Right hand
more or fewer than 4 arrows, 8 rays or 2 hands
any text beyond the twelve listed labels, and any letter other than E in red on the compass card
images.takeaway: Facing the rising Sun is facing east: her left hand points north, her right hand points south and west is behind her.
images.description: A girl seen from above facing the rising Sun on the right, with her arms stretched up and down the frame and the four directions marked around her.
images.context: Concept image for Finding Directions by the Rising Sun. It follows the idea of the opener of your maths book (a child who faces the rising Sun with the compass rose beside) and uses this concept's own girl, Lali, seen from above.
images.teaching_notes: Turn the page in your head: with north at the top, a girl who faces east looks to the right, so her left hand is at the top. Let the student say each direction aloud. The slip to watch: thinking the left hand always points west.

image_decisions.why: Seen from above, the girl, the Sun and the four arrows make east in front, north on the left hand, south on the right hand and west behind countable, which words alone do not show.
